description: Evaluation scenarios for the engineering planner skill. Each scenario tests a distinct capability.

evals.name: Micro plan — targeted single-file change
evals.query: Add rate limiting to the /api/export endpoint
expected_behavior: Classifies as Micro (single endpoint, one middleware, < 4h)
Produces a checklist plan, not a full PLAN.md
Every checklist item has a concrete acceptance criterion
States at least 1 non-goal (e.g., not rate-limiting other endpoints)
Identifies rate limiter storage (Redis vs in-memory) as a dependency or open question
Names a specific file path for the middleware
Does not overengineer — no phases, no architecture section

evals.name: Standard plan — new feature with frontend and backend
evals.query: Build a CSV export feature for the reports page
expected_behavior: Classifies as Standard (backend API + frontend component, 2-3 days)
Writes PLAN-csv-export.md to disk
Goal is observable: specifies row limit, response time, or format requirement
Technical design names real or plausible file paths (API route, component, utility)
At least 2 alternatives considered (client-side vs server-side, streaming vs buffered)
Risk: memory usage on large exports is identified
Testing strategy includes integration test for the endpoint, not just 'write tests'
Phase breakdown: Backend, Frontend, Polish/Tests with day estimates
Non-goals include at least 'Excel format' and 'scheduled exports'
First action in summary is concrete and immediately startable

evals.name: Epic plan — database migration
evals.query: Migrate our application from MongoDB to PostgreSQL
expected_behavior: Classifies as Epic (cross-cutting migration, multiple phases, week+)
Uses RFC-style template with Goals, Background, Architecture, Phases
At least 3 phases with exit criteria for each
Risks include data loss (High likelihood, High impact = Score 9) with mitigation
Rollback strategy defined
Dependencies: DBA, DevOps, infra, all teams using DB
Alternatives considered: staying on MongoDB, using a hybrid approach
Operations section with monitoring and alerts
Open questions about data volume, migration downtime tolerance, and team availability
Testing strategy includes data integrity validation, not just unit tests

evals.name: Ambiguous request — should ask before planning
expected_behavior: Does NOT immediately produce a plan
Asks exactly ONE focused clarifying question (not multiple)
The question asks what 'faster' means: which flows, what baseline, what target metric
Does not ask about implementation details — only about the goal
After question is answered (or assumptions are stated), proceeds with a plan

evals.name: Quick-plan mode — respects user's explicit brevity request
evals.query: Give me a quick rough plan for adding OAuth2 login
expected_behavior: Detects 'quick' and 'rough' → uses Micro format regardless of actual OAuth complexity
Explicitly states it is using quick-plan mode
Produces a checklist, not a full PLAN.md with phases
Still includes at least one acceptance criterion per task
Still identifies the top risk (token storage, redirect URI, provider choice)
Does NOT produce a full RFC or epic plan

evals.name: New/empty project — no existing codebase
evals.query: Plan the initial architecture for a task management REST API in Node.js
expected_behavior: Detects that no codebase exists yet (empty directory or no source files)
Does NOT fail or produce a generic non-plan
All file paths in technical design are marked 'to be created'
Recommends a directory structure
Identifies key tech choices as open questions (ORM, auth library, DB)
Standard or Epic scale — not Micro (new API = multi-day)
Goal is observable: e.g., 'All CRUD endpoints for tasks respond correctly under Postman smoke test'

evals.name: Should NOT trigger — debugging an existing error
evals.query: The login endpoint is returning 500, help me debug it
expected_behavior: Skill does NOT auto-trigger
Claude handles this as a normal debugging request, not a planning request
No PLAN file is created

evals.name: Should NOT trigger — trivial code review
evals.query: Can you review this function for correctness?
expected_behavior: Skill does NOT auto-trigger
Claude handles as code review, not planning
No PLAN file is created

quality_thresholds.notes: All critical evals must pass. Quick-mode and new-project evals are important but secondary. Trigger-negative evals depend on Claude's skill selection, not skill execution.
